title: Investigate and remediate real-time vs reconstructed per-model peaks divergence in Console charts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Over the last three weeks we've observed persistent divergence between the real-time streaming usage lines and reconstructed (ledger-based) per-model peak traces in the Console 'Top Models' chart for a subset of tenants. Divergence takes the form of short (~5-30 minute) positive spikes in reconstructed traces that have no corresponding events in the real-time stream, and occasional negative dips when a backfill replay removes previously attributed tokens. This ticket investigates root causes and implements fixes to ensure reconstructed aggregates match streaming view within agreed tolerance (<=1% hourly delta) and to eliminate customer-facing regressions after late ingests/backfills.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-25: Initial triage by telemetry team (Ava) - flagged from internal SLO alert: per-model hourly delta > 10% for 4 customers between streaming_feed and ledger_reconstructed aggregates.

2026-02-27: Pulled sample tenant audit (tenant_alpha): found late shard replays originating from shard-replayer service GC window; late events had sequence_ids but were missing ingestion_uuid header leading to no de-dup at reconstruction stage.

2026-03-01: Correlated spikes to rate-limit credit adjustments: dedicated-tenant burst credits were retroactively applied by billing-ledger job which mutates allocation_weight on historical tokens during commit; this causes reconstructed aggregation to add buckets after the fact.

2026-03-04: Frontend smoothing misalignment: chart smoothing window aligns to dashboard refresh time rather than event_time. When reconstruction inserts retroactive tokens the smoothing algorithm computed on client produced negative dips due to inconsistent time alignment.

2026-03-07: Reproducer created - synthetic ingestion pipeline produced late events (simulated network partition) and replayed into ledger; observed duplicate token attribution when ingestion_uuid missing; sample scripts and datasets uploaded to Drive (link in attachments).

2026-03-10: Hypothesis: two independent issues - (1) missing ingestion UUID and weak dedup logic during reconstruction, (2) mutation of historical allocation_weight by billing job without emitting compensating reconciliation events. Both amplify when smoothing window is misaligned in the UI.

2026-03-12: Confirmed cause-of-duplicates: shard-replayer retries used a different canonical_id and the ledger merge used a last-writer-wins on allocation_weight, not an additive adjustment; ledger_rebuild job lacks idempotent check for replayed sequences.

2026-03-13: Discussed with Billing (Leila Morgan) and Runtime (Ravi Patel) - agreed to stop retroactive allocation_weight edits without an audit delta event and to add ingestion_uuid propagation from gateway to ledger.
2026-03-14: Plan reviewed and approved by SRE and PM (Nina Roberts). Code owners assigned for reconstruction job and frontend chart smoothing.

Artifact links: console dashboard (internal) - https://console.internal/redwood/top-models; reproducer dataset (Drive) - https://drive.redwood/repro/late-events.zip; initial PR draft - https://github.com/redwood/recon/pull/1428
root_cause_summary: Two interacting defects: (A) Reconstruction pipeline did not reliably deduplicate late/replayed events because ingestion UUID was not mandatory and the idempotency key was sometimes different on retries; (B) Billing-ledger job applied allocation_weight corrections in-place on historical records instead of emitting reconciliation deltas, so reconstructed aggregates changed retroactively without a clear audit trail. The Console's smoothing logic then exaggerated visual artifacts when event_time and render_time diverged.
decision_log: Make ingestion_uuid required at gateway and propagate to downstream tenants and ledger. Backfill existing records with best-effort UUIDs only for internal reconciliation where safe.

Change billing-ledger to emit explicit 'allocation_delta' reconciliation events rather than mutating historical allocation_weight. These deltas will be applied via the same reconstruction pipeline as regular token events so they are visible to streaming metrics and have an audit id.

Modify reconstruction job to perform idempotent merge by using (ingestion_uuid, sequence_id, tenant_id) tuple and skip events already applied. Add a small tombstone TTL for removed duplicates to prevent reapplication during backfill windows.
Adjust Console smoothing algorithm to window on event_time and make smoothing alignment configurable; surface 'data backfilled' marker if any backfilled events are applied older than 72 hours.
Introduce a 'reconciliation-mode' for the first run where we run reconstruction in dry-run and produce a diff report to validate before committing changes to the ledger.
Rollout plan: internal canary -> staging -> 100% once diff metrics under thresholds.
proposed_work_items: ENG: Add ingestion_uuid enforcement to API gateway and return 400 if missing for new ingests (gateway change) - assignee: Miguel
ENG: Update reconstruction Spark job to deduplicate on (ingestion_uuid, sequence_id, tenant) and add dry-run mode (recon repo) - assignee: Priya S.
BILLING: Stop in-place allocation_weight edits and emit allocation_delta events instead (billing-ledger service) - assignee: Leila Morgan
ENG: Add reconciliation-run tooling to produce human-readable diff report and a reversed-apply path for safe rollback - assignee: Ravi
FE: Change chart smoothing to event_time alignment and add UI marker for backfilled data (console frontend) - assignee: Hana Kim
QA: Create synthetic test harness to simulate late replays and assert streaming vs reconstructed delta <1% hourly - assignee: QA Team
implementation_notes: Reconstruction: introduce state table 'applied_events_v2' keyed by (tenant, ingestion_uuid, sequence_id) with 'applied_at' timestamp. This table is append-only; deletions use tombstones so we can still compact later. Store only hashes to limit storage growth.

Billing: add producer for allocation_delta events. Fields: tenant_id, model_id, delta_tokens, reason, source_job_id, audit_id. Emitted deltas consumed by the same reconstruction pipeline so they show up in reconstructed aggregates in the same code path.

Frontend: smoothing change will be behind feature flag 'console.smoothing.event_time' initially. When enabled, smoothing uses event_time aligned windows. Also surface a small tooltip: 'Some values shown are from backfilled events applied after ingestion.'

Backward compatibility: gateway will accept older clients without ingestion_uuid for 30 days but will tag them as 'legacy' and route into a separate reconciliation queue to avoid immediate double-counting. After 30-day window we will enforce 400 errors.
Migration window: run dry-run recon on a 72-hour sliding window and produce diffs. Expect ~0.2% of tokens to reassign for most tenants; any tenant >5% flagged for manual review.
Performance: dedup checks will add a point lookup per event. We'll batch lookups in memory per partition and use Bloom filter heuristic to reduce DB load.
Observability: add reconciliation metrics: recon_diff_tokens, recon_diff_pct, deduped_event_count, allocation_delta_count. Add dashboards and pager rules if recon_diff_pct > 5% sustained for 1h.
Safety: large historical runs (>30 days) require Runbook signoff and manual throttling to avoid DB IOPS storms.
testing_qa: Unit tests for dedup logic (ingestion_uuid missing/slightly different canonical ids)
Integration test: simulate gateway replay + billing delta emission and assert single final attribution per sequence_id
Staging job: run reconstruction dry-run for last 7 days, review diff report, and sample tenants in slack channel #recon-audit
Visual test: enable smoothing.event_time FF in staging and validate charts do not show negative dips after backfill runs
Canary: rollout to 10% of tenants with low churn for 48 hours and verify recon_diff_pct < 1% and no alert fires
rollout_and_monitoring: Phase 1 (internal): apply gateway and reconstruction dry-run on internal tenants - 3 days
Phase 2 (staging): enable allocation_delta emission and run dry-run recon across staging - 4 days
Phase 3 (canary): enable features for 10% tenants and monitor recon_diff_pct, chart anomaly rate, and user complaints - 48 hours
Phase 4 (global): full rollout if canary metrics OK. Post-rollout: weekly audit for 4 weeks to ensure no regressions.
Key metrics: streaming_vs_recon_token_diff_pct (goal <=1%), deduped_event_count, allocation_delta_count, console_chart_anomaly_rate
Alerting: create pager for recon_diff_pct > 5% sustained 1 hour (SRE Pager)
Postmortem: if any tenant experiences >10% token reassignments, block rollout and open incident review.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Large historical reconciliation may cause DB/IO spikes. Mitigation: rate-limit backfill, use batched windows, and require runbook approval for >7-day runs.
Risk: Changing gateway to require ingestion_uuid may break older SDKs. Mitigation: 30-day grace period, legac y routing queue, and proactive customer comms.
Risk: Allocation deltas may not fully capture prior business logic (billing rounding). Mitigation: run parity checks against billing reports and involve Finance for validation.
Risk: Frontend FF may introduce minor visual differences. Mitigation: default FF off, compare before/after snapshots, and revert quickly if user impact seen.
